title: Bayes Rules! An Introduction to Applied Bayesian Modeling
description: Applied Bayesian statistics textbook in R (rstan, rstanarm, bayesplot and the bayesrules package), online edition. Unit I Bayesian Foundations (the Bayesian picture, Bayes' rule, Beta-Binomial model, balance and sequentiality, conjugate families); Unit II Posterior Simulation & Analysis (approximating the posterior, MCMC under the hood, posterior inference and prediction); Unit III Bayesian Regression & Classification (simple normal regression; evaluating regression models with posterior predictive checks, cross-validation and expected log-predictive density; extensions; Poisson and negative binomial; logistic; naive Bayes); Unit IV Hierarchical Bayesian models (complete, no and partial pooling; normal hierarchical models without and with predictors; non-normal hierarchical models; more layers).
rightsNotes: Preface, License section (2026-10-31): 'This work is licensed under a Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 4.0 International License.'

The home page notes the book is 'now available in print by CRC Press'; the print edition is commercial and was not examined. The preface cautions that some bayesrules package datasets may be biased and are not for rigorous research; the package itself was not audited.

Chapter 1 The Big (Bayesian) Picture: 1.1 Thinking like a Bayesian; 1.2 A quick history lesson; 1.3 A look ahead; 1.4 Chapter summary; 1.5 Exercises

Chapter 10 Evaluating Regression Models: 10.1 Is the model fair?; 10.2 How wrong is the model? (posterior predictive checks); 10.3 How accurate are the posterior predictive models? (10.3.2 Cross-validation; 10.3.3 Expected log-predictive density); 10.4 How good is the MCMC simulation vs how good is the model?; exercises; model comparison deferred to Section 11.5
Chapter 15 Hierarchical Models are Exciting: 15.1 Complete pooling; 15.2 No pooling; 15.3 Hierarchical data; 15.4 Partial pooling with hierarchical models; 15.5 Chapter summary; 15.6 Exercises
limitations: Undergraduate applied level ('not written at the graduate level' per the preface); the mathematics is lighter than a mathematically confident learner may want.
Code and exercises use R and Stan; Corniversity's Python labs need their own implementations.
Identifiability, parameter recovery and model recovery were not found in the chapters opened; model comparison is introduced through ELPD (10.3.3) and treated in Section 11.5, which was not opened.
Only Chapters 1, 10 and 15 were opened; the others are known from the contents.
